title: Creatify vs Hiring an AI Ad Agency: Which Should You Buy?
summary: Creatify software vs an AI ad agency: who writes, checks and uploads the ads, what each costs on published pages, and which model fits your team.
body_markdown:
## Other providers: Creatify Studio, Airpost, Admiral Media and MakeUGC


### Creatify Studio: the managed route from the same vendor


Studio is the closest option to Creatify's own platform. The[Studio page](https://creatify.ai/studio) describes an assigned creative strategist, a team that uses AI to write hooks and scripts, AI plus human QA on every asset, and a 48-hour turnaround. It does not say whether Studio runs campaigns, so ask before you sign. Studio suits a team that likes Creatify's output but has no time to operate the platform.


### Airpost: a dedicated AI video team that uploads to your Meta account


Airpost's[pricing page](https://www.airpost.ai/pricing) lists a platform plus a dedicated AI video team from $6,000 a month. Its listed work includes product animation, UGC-style ads and short hooks. It uploads ads to your Meta account, and its homepage describes running tests and scale campaigns. The page describes 10 to 100+ ads, so confirm the monthly count in your plan.


### Admiral Media: fixed AI UGC batches


Admiral Media sells creator-style video ads for apps and ecommerce brands, made with AI presenters and finished with human editing and quality review. Its[AI UGC page](https://admiral.media/ai-ugc-agency/) lists Starter at €10,000 for 20 ads, Growth at €16,000 for 40 and Pro at €29,000 for 80. It says ideal clients invest US$50,000 or more a month in paid media, and that campaign and budget management is agreed separately. The same page says AI UGC is scripted advertising, not content from a real customer.


### MakeUGC: self-serve AI actors with a managed option


MakeUGC lists talking AI actors that can hold your product, with Starter at $29 a month billed yearly for 500 credits. As of October 2026, it also advertises a managed Enterprise option. Choose the self-serve plan when you want to operate the tool, and ask for the Enterprise scope in writing if you want the work done for you.


## Which should you choose: software or an agency?


Decide by who does the weekly work, using three checks:


- **Weekly hours.** Software needs someone to write scripts, rerun weak takes and review claims every week. If nobody has those hours, the platform will stall and finished ads are the safer buy.
- **Volume.** Creatify lists 11 fifteen-second avatar videos for the 55 credits on its $15 Standard plan, which suits a test. A weekly refresh calls for either many plan credits or a team that produces a steady batch.
- **Review.** A self-serve tool leaves the final check with you. An agency or a managed service such as Creatify Studio moves part of that check to its team, but you still approve claims before they run.


If you like Creatify's output but lack the time, Studio is the nearest managed step. If you also want Meta campaigns handled, ask each provider in writing whether that is included.


## Who checks the claims, owns the account and labels the ad?


Whichever route you pick, you still answer for accuracy. Creatify's[URL to Video workflow](https://creatify.ai/features/url-to-video) turns a product link into a draft ad, so review the extracted claims, assets and generated script yourself. Meta's[Ad Creative Generative AI Terms](https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/ad_creative_generative_ai_terms) make the advertiser solely responsible for checking the accuracy of output from Meta's own tools. Ask an agency how it checks claims before the first batch ships.


The account is the second check. Ask an agency to work inside an ad account your business owns. Meta's[help center](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1717412048538897) has an article on giving a partner access to business assets in your business portfolio. Keep your ad account, pixel and Pages in your own portfolio, give the agency access rather than ownership, and confirm the access level in writing.


The third check is the label. Meta says it labels ads[created or significantly edited with its own generative AI features](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) , and that the label appears when those tools add a photorealistic AI-generated person. It also says it will detect ads made with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label, but its post does not say that detection is live yet. Ask each provider how it plans for that label.


Volume is the fourth question. Meta's[Andromeda engineering post](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/02/production-engineering/meta-andromeda-advantage-automation-next-gen-personalized-ads-retrieval-engine/) says the number of ad creatives in its systems is expected to grow significantly. Count distinct concepts, meaning the angle and proof behind each ad, not the files delivered. Re-cuts of one idea test the same angle twice.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick if you want finished Facebook and Instagram ads each week without running software, with optional Meta campaign management or creative only.
- Creatify fits a team that will write scripts, run the platform and check every claim, with paid plans from $15 a month.
- Creatify Studio is the closest Creatify option to an agency, but its page does not say whether it runs campaigns.
- Compare providers on the cost of one approved ad from the same brief, not on plan price or credits.
- Ask every provider who checks claims, who owns the ad account and how it handles AI labels.


## FAQ


### Is Creatify cheaper than hiring an AI ad agency?


Creatify's paid plans start at $15 a month, while Airpost lists its dedicated team from $6,000 a month. The two prices buy different things: generations on one side, and finished ads with a team on the other. Divide each total by the number of approved ads, and count your own scripting and review hours in the software option.


### Can Creatify Studio run my Meta campaigns?


Creatify's Studio page does not say whether Studio runs campaigns, so ask in writing before you sign. If you need campaign management too, confirm whether it is included or priced separately. Knowlify offers optional end-to-end Meta campaign management, or creative only for teams with their own buyer.


### Who should own the Meta ad account?


Your business should own the ad account, pixel and Pages, and give the agency access rather than ownership. Meta's help center has an article on how to give a partner access to business assets in your business portfolio. Confirm that arrangement in writing before the first ad goes live.


### Do AI presenter ads need a label on Facebook and Instagram?


Meta says it labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI tools when they add a photorealistic AI-generated person. It says it will also detect third-party AI-made ads and label them "AI info", but its post does not confirm that detection is live. Ask each provider how it handles the label before you commit.
